title: Resiliency orchestrator Terraform module for priv VPC EKS control plane
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (and accompanying CI playbook) that provisions Redwood Private EKS control-plane resources inside customer VPCs with robust resiliency primitives. Module responsibilities: declarative control plane stack composition, cross-account KMS/IAM wiring for encrypted secrets, preflight validations, idempotent apply patterns, automated canary and staged control-plane upgrades, continuous health probes and self-healing hooks (restart/cordon/drain guardrail), drift detection telemetry, and safe rollback primitives. The module should integrate with existing provisioning operator and expose outputs consumed by the private controlplane operator and onboarding playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published to registry with semantic versioning and example usage for priv VPC EKS control plane
Idempotent applies: repeated Terraform apply on module produces no diffs when cluster is healthy
Preflight checks: network, subnets, route tables, KMS access and IAM roles validated with clear error messages
Upgrade orchestration: canary promotion flow implemented via tagging and a staged lifecycle plan; rollback path validated in staging
Health probes: control-plane liveness/readiness checks runable from observability agent and surface Prometheus metrics and CloudWatch logs
Observability: provisioning telemetry flows to Console dashboard with per-stage timing and failure reasons
Security: cross-account KMS keys are created following least-privilege patterns and documented key rotation steps
E2E test: automated CI job that provisions a short-lived control plane in a sandbox VPC and runs the health and upgrade smoke tests
tasks: Design module public interface and variables with backwards-compatibility for existing provisioning composer
Implement resource graph: eksctl/eks modules wrapper, managed node IAM roles for control-plane, kms resources, s3 for state if needed
Add preflight validations for VPC configuration and KMS access using terraform external/local-exec checks
Implement staged upgrade mechanism using lifecycle tags and external canary controller integration
Add dynamic health probes that register with observability (prometheus cloudwatch exporters) and signals for reconcilers
Write unit and integration tests in Terratest; add CI workflow that runs tests in ephemeral AWS accounts
Create docs: usage examples, rollback playbook, runbook for oncall
Security review and KMS/IAM least-privilege signoff
progress_updates: 2025-01-12: RFC drafted and shared with infra-sigs; initial module variable schema defined
2025-01-18: POC for preflight checks implemented using terraform null_resource + local-exec; verified failure modes in bare sandbox
2025-01-22: Discussion with Security on cross-account KMS patterns; agreed to use separate customer-managed key per account and a restricted grant model
2025-01-27: First Terratest harness committed (creates ephemeral VPC + controlplane stub); CI runner flakiness observed, investigating cause
2025-01-30: Added health probe exporter stub and wiring to console dashboard prototype; updated acceptance criteria to include prometheus metrics
review_feedback: PM review (R. Chen): emphasize minimal blast radius for canary upgrades and strong defaults for timeouts
Design review (N. Patel): prefer declarative lifecycle tags over imperative scripts for staged promotion; reduces operator surface
Security review (L. Gomez): require KMS key rotation notes in README and add terraform-provider-aws kms key policy template
Infra review (S. Becker): suggest adding jittered retry and exponential backoff for preflight network checks to avoid transient failures
risks: State drift between Terraform and operator reconciliation leading to conflicted control-plane configuration
KMS cross-account misconfiguration could break access to encrypted secrets during upgrades
CI fragility: ephemeral account provisioning may fail intermittently and mask regressions
Rollbacks may require manual intervention for certain failure modes (e.g., IAM role corruption)
next_steps: Stabilize Terratest CI and add retries for known flakey AWS API errors
Implement canary promotion controller prototype and wire into stage tags
Finish KMS policy templates and run security tabletop in 2025-W05
Prepare a staged rollout: start with internal sandbox tenants, then opt-in early customers, followed by default for new accounts
